messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty: Triggered alert 'api-inference-5xx-spike' for service=redwood-hosted-api severity=high -> https://pagerduty.local/incidents/PD12345 :rotating_light:
incident-bot: primary on-call jamal paged (sms + mobile push)
incident-bot: escalation: secondary sara will be paged in 2m if unacked
jamal: On it, getting phone. Seeing a bunch of 502s in the logs, looks like tokenization workers choking.
sara: I didn't get the page yet. If jamal doesn't ack within 90s, PD will escalate to me.
jamal: ack 4476543210 - taking ownership. quick triage: 502s from /v1/generate with backend error E_PIPE_OVERFLOW on gpu-node-7.
kevin: copying logs, looks like repeated OOM spikes on kvcache allocation around the same time. snippet:
```
2026-03-15T03:12:47Z ERROR worker.py OOMError: failed to reserve 512MB KV cache
2026-03-15T03:12:47Z ERROR request_handler.py Traceback (most recent call last):
  File \"/app/handler.py\", line 201, in handle
    out = model.generate(req)
OOMError: KVCache allocation failed
```
jamal: thanks. I'm going to route traffic off gpu-node-7 and trigger a restart of the inference service on that host. @ops-manager can you stand by for rollback if restart fails?
ops-manager: standing by. also paging manager per escalation policy in case restart doesn't clear within 5m.
sara: PD escalation fired: manager paged (ops-lead Maria) - PD incident PD12345 escalated after missed secondary ack window.
maria: I'm on the manager page, joining the thread. tagging for impact assessment: which customers and routes affected?
jamal: initial estimate: customers with long-context generation /enterprise routes hit ~15% error rate, public test users intermittent 502s. rate spike started at 03:12 UTC.
kevin: mitigation step 1 completed: drained traffic from gpu-node-7 -> load balancer shows node healthy false. step 2: restart attempt 1 in progress (systemctl restart redwood-inference).
jamal: restart returned healthy processes but memory pressure still high on node. continuing to monitor. if errors persist I'll shift canary traffic to dedicated pool.
sara: PD: ack escalation to manager shown as delivered. manager confirmed monitoring.
ops-manager: if restart doesn't work in 3m, we should replace node from pool and rehydrate from snapshot. also please open an incident bridge: use /zoom create and add infra and ml-runtime.
maria: opening bridge and invite ops, ml-runtime, product-support. bridge: https://zoom.local/bridge/INC-PD12345
kevin: restart didn't clear OOMs. scheduling node replacement now. container will be rescheduled to gpu-node-12.
jamal: rerouted ~60% of traffic to dedicated-pool as temporary measure. errors down to ~3% now.
sara: great. can we confirm there was no customer data loss? any failed requests that could have retried with charges?
kevin: no data loss; errors were 502s, requests never completed. billing team: please see incident notes for retry rules.
maria: good work. next steps: 1) replace node + verify KV cache config, 2) increase soft limits on KV allocator, 3) postmortem timeline and customer communication draft. tagging @product-support to prepare an advisory if enterprise SLAs affected.
jamal: leaving an on-call handoff note: I'm handing off active mitigation to sara at 03:16 UTC since I'm taking a quick break. sara, you own the follow-ups and PD updates.
sara: taking over. updating PagerDuty note: 'ack by jamal, escalated to manager, traffic rerouted, node replacement in progress, no data loss, partial customer impact (15%->3% errors)'.
incident-bot: PagerDuty note updated for PD12345 by sara.
maria: thanks team. keep the bridge open until postmortem triage. I'll coordinate customer comms once we have root cause analysis. :thumbsup:
kevin: node replacement finished, kube rescheduled, KV alloc limits bumped. monitoring shows stable memory and errors at 0.5% baseline.
sara: closing mitigation loop: adding tasks to incident board and scheduling postmortem for 2026-03-15 10:00 UTC.
jamal: back, thanks for takeover. will add runbook improvements to postmortem.
maria: closing note: PD incident will be assigned severity s2. Customer-impact summary to be attached to the postmortem. great job. :clap:
